milestones.milestone: 1. A sentence → a registered simulated robot → validated destination → permission → goal → **ROS 2 and Nav2 execute it in Gazebo** → real feedback → cancel → independent verification
milestones.state: Every step except Gazebo and Nav2 is verified with the built-in simulator. The ROS 2 adapter, the Gazebo robot and the container are written and have never been run. **Not met** until the Gazebo acceptance check passes (blocker B1)

milestones.milestone: 2. The same on a physical robot, after commissioning
milestones.state: **Not started.** The commissioning procedure exists and is tested with a stand-in; no robot has been commissioned (blocker B2)

milestones.milestone: 3. A second class of hardware (an arm), with a dedicated manipulation integration
milestones.state: **Partly.** A pick and place, step by step and as one plan, is verified with HANNAH's built-in arm simulator. MoveIt 2 with a real or Gazebo arm is not started (blocker B3)

limitations: Everything runs against simulators written for this project. They are kinematic: no physics, friction, wheel slip, sensor noise models, or the timing of a real machine.
The planner in the simulator is not Nav2, and the arm simulator is not MoveIt 2. Behaviour in Gazebo and on hardware will differ.
Position is odometry (drifting) corrected only in the dock. There is no map-based localization in the simulator.
Perception is range-sensor geometry and regions of colour in a simulated camera's picture. HANNAH cannot say what an object is, and nothing identifies a person.
The arm simulator is planar, with no dynamics, payload or grasp physics; its objects come from its own scene, not from a camera.
One robot per runtime; one account per robot; missions of minutes, not hours. HANNAH has no workspaces or organizations.
Commands reach a robot at its next exchange (about a second). Anything needing a faster reaction belongs to the robot's controller.
A physical robot's every movement needs approval, and it is refused a plan of several steps. There is no scoped autonomy for hardware.
The Stop button is a software request. It is not, and cannot be made into, an emergency stop. HANNAH is not safety-certified.
No live language model has driven the robot agents; their tools and instructions are tested with a scripted server. Voice requests for robots are untested.
Webhook deliveries for robot events are best effort and are not retried.
The app's Robots screen is tested in a desktop browser at desktop and phone widths, not on a phone or in the desktop app.
